comments: Return the Memberships inheritable from supertypes of this Type with redefined Features removed. When computing inheritable Memberships, exclude Imports of excludedNamespaces, Specializations of excludedTypes, and, if excludeImplied = true, all implied Specializations.

Return a subset of memberships, removing those Memberships whose memberElements are Features and for which either of the following two conditions holds:

  1. The memberElement of the Membership is included in redefined Features of another Membership in memberships.
  2. One of the redefined Features of the Membership is a directly redefinedFeature of an ownedFeature of this Type.

For this purpose, the redefined Features of a Membership whose memberElement is a Feature includes the memberElement and all Features directly or indirectly redefined by the memberElement.
bodies: let reducedMemberships : Sequence(Membership) =     memberships->reject(mem1 |         memberships->excluding(mem1)->             exists(mem2 | allRedefinedFeaturesOf(mem2)->                 includes(mem1.memberElement))) in let redefinedFeatures : Set(Feature) =      ownedFeature.redefinition.redefinedFeature->asSet() in reducedMemberships->reject(mem | allRedefinedFeaturesOf(mem)->     exists(feature | redefinedFeatures->includes(feature)))

interpretation: A Type is also a Namespace. An explicit member FeatureElement is owned through OwningMembership, without owningFeatureMembership or owningType. Its lexical containing Type must not add feature, parameter, return, portion or contextual Step roles.
Static Feature.type still uses its own typing, subsetting and last chaining feature through the common checked reducer. Expression.result still comes from the Expression membership proof.

Ordinary owned namespace members and foreign aliases use the same reciprocal ownership certificate and redefinition reduction; neither becomes a feature merely because its containing namespace is a Type.

An ordinary member of an end Feature can be its owned cross feature. The prototype requires complete evidence that the enclosing Feature is not an end; true or malformed flags remain incomplete until the crossing obligations are separately supported.

Type.removeRedefinedFeatures compares local ownedFeature redefinition targets, not all locally owned namespace members. A TypeFeatureMember redefinition does not immediately suppress the inherited original. At the next inheritance level both memberships are incoming, so their shared redefinition closure suppresses the original. A locally owned FeatureMembership also suppresses it directly. The common reducer already implements this distinction; the initial new test expectation was incorrect.
